title: No double counting: a reopened case counts one outcome and a takeover is not AI-resolved
risk: A reopened case is counted twice and a taken-over session is still credited to the AI, so the automation rate improves exactly as human effort increases.
preconditions: Namespace gov-kpi-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the metric is computed by the real reporting code over fixtures/offline/governance.json kpi_dataset and never copied from the dashboard payload.

Frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z with the reporting window 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2026-02-01T00:00:00Z as a half-open interval; the stored aggregate is recomputed independently from the raw counter rows.
kpi_edge.reopen_and_takeover describes one reopened case and three taken-over sessions inside the same window.
The case model keeps a single case identity across a reopen, and a takeover transfers the affected leg's credit to the human.

reopen_and_takeover.expected: one final outcome per reopened case and no AI-resolved credit for a taken-over session

steps.action: Reopen the closed case and close it again with a final outcome
steps.expected: The case keeps one identity, the reopen is recorded once with its delta from the AI closure, and the final outcome replaces the earlier outcome instead of adding a second one.

steps.action: Read the AI resolution numerator after the reopen
steps.expected: The case is not counted twice; if a human resolved the reopened case, the AI resolution numerator loses it.

steps.action: Take over three sessions and re-read the counters
steps.expected: Those sessions are credited to the human, the AI resolution numerator does not gain them, and the human override counter increases by the number of overridden sessions.

steps.action: Attempt to count the reopened case as a new case
steps.expected: The attempt is refused, and the case count plus the reopen flag stay consistent with the case identity.

assertions: Each case contributes exactly one final outcome, so the case count does not grow when a case is reopened.
A taken-over session is never credited to AI resolution, and the transferred weight is visible on the human side.
The reopen rate uses AI-closed cases as its denominator and counts a reopen only once, within 72 hours of the AI closure.
AI resolution rate and human override rate move in opposite directions when a takeover happens, so the two metrics cannot both improve from the same event.
forbidden: Counting a reopened case as a second case to inflate the closure count.
Crediting a taken-over session to the AI because the AI handled the early turns.
Dropping the reopen flag after the second closure so the quality signal disappears.
evidence: Case identity history with the reopen delta and the final outcome.
AI resolution and human override counters before and after the takeover.
Reopen report listing the case once with its flag.
cleanup: Delete gov- case history, takeover records and aggregate rows after export.
automation: The reporting service and the metric dictionary run as real code under test over the frozen KPI dataset; the dashboard is a consumer whose displayed value must equal the independently recomputed value. Waits are condition-based on the stored aggregate row, metric values are never supplied as inputs, and no vendor boundary is involved in the arithmetic.
